result.title: On Demand, Not Uniformity: Adaptive Expert Orchestration for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
result.summary: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) enables Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to adapt to sequential instruction data while retaining previously acquired knowledge. While recent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based methods mitigate forgetting by freezing historical experts and introducing new ones, they largely overlook the varying adaptation demands across tasks. Probing incoming tasks reveals pronounced heterogeneity in layer-wise gradient pressure and token-wise prediction difficulty. This observation highlights two unresolved decisions: where additional capacity is needed and how strongly new experts should contribute to individual tokens. To address both questions, we propose the Coverage-Calibrated Expert Injection and Residual Arbitration framework (CIRA-MoE), which derives expert acceptance margins via learnable threshold routing to serve as a unified coverage signal. Specifically, historical acceptance evidence guides the selective injection of new experts into insufficiently covered layers. Meanwhile, relative evidence between historical and current experts modulates token-wise residual contributions, coupled with arbitration-consistent regularization to promote expert specialization. Comprehensive experiments on UCIT and CoIN demonstrate that CIRA-MoE outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in MCIT.

AI.brief_summary: 针对多模态持续指令微调中的灾难性遗忘，基于层间梯度压力与逐 token 难度异质性，用可学习阈值路由形成覆盖率信号，决定在何处注入新专家以及新专家对每个 token 的残差贡献强度，并在 UCIT、CoIN 上取得优于现有方法的性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作本身服务于持续微调的防遗忘，不涉及视觉证据保留或 latent 推理状态生成；但其「历史证据驱动的逐 token 残差仲裁与容量按需注入」或可为 LVR 中按 token 分配计算与调制不同来源贡献提供机制线索，值得核查。
